Analytics Methodology & Technical Framework

The SupeRR Selector pressure analysis engine evaluates delivery-level performance against empirical expected-value baselines constructed from all qualifying IPL and T20I matches (2022 onward). Ratings standardize performance over expected outcomes and apply empirical Bayesian shrinkage toward zero.

1. Expected-Value Baselines (Task 1)

413 discrete game-state buckets across all 2022+ competition balls. Second innings is partitioned by balls remaining [1-6, 7-12, 13-24, 25-36, 37-60, 61-120], Required Run Rate (RRR) in 0.5 rpo intervals (capped at 16+), and wickets in hand [1-3, 4-6, 7-10]. First innings incorporates match phase and venue par tertiles (<165, 165-185, >185).

2. Pressure Definitions (Task 2)

Batters: 2nd innings deliveries with RRR ≥ 9.0 or death overs (overs 16-20 / balls rem ≤ 30) in either innings.
Bowlers: 2nd innings core chase band (RRR 8.0-12.0) and last-over component (balls rem 1-6). Balls in both count once exclusively in last-over.

3. Dual Ranking Engine (Task 5)

Set A (Global): Evaluates every qualifying player in the 2022+ dataset, standardizing z-scores against all qualifying players.
Set B (RR Only): Filters to players who appeared for Rajasthan Royals, standardizing z-scores against the RR squad pool for internal franchise consistency.

4. Formulas & Sample Rules (Tasks 3, 4, 5)

Batters: Rating = z(Runs Above Expected/100) − z(Dismissal Penalty). Shrinkage: (Balls × Raw) / (Balls + 30). Min sample: 30 pressure balls.
Bowlers: Rating = z(Runs Saved/Ov) + z(Wicket Comp) + 0.5 × z(Last Over Comp). Shrinkage: (Balls × Raw) / (Balls + 24). Min sample: 24 band balls.

Data pack for competition use only. Not for publication. • Rajasthan Royals • SupeRR Selector Season 2
